 JUDGMENT "In declaring that claimant No.1 in LAC No.90/2006 is entitled to receive the award amount,
whether the Reference Court committed illegality and perversity?" is the question involved in this case.
2. The appellant was respondent No.3(d), respondent No.2 was claimant No.1, respondent No.3 was claimant No.2, M.C.Bhaskar the father of the appellant was claimant No.3, respondent Nos.7 to 9 were claimant Nos.4 to 6 and respondent No.1 was the first respondent in LAC No.90/2006 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Devanahalli.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Reference court.

3. The land bearing Sy.No.32 measuring 4 acre of Anneshwara village was acquired under the final notification dated 08.08.1996 issued under Section 28(4) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board Act, 1966 (for short 'K.I.A.D.B. Act') for the purpose of forming of the International Airport, Devanahalli.

sentences.text: The Special Land Acquisition Officer/respondent No.1 passed an award dated 22.01.2002 awarding compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
Claimant No.1 had the laid claim for compensation amount as the owner and in occupation of the land.
4. M.C.Bhaskar respondent No.3 filed objections before the Land Acquisition Officer claiming that he is entitled to receive the compensation.
He claimed that the land was granted to him by the Government under Ex.P18.
Claimant No.1 contended that after such grant of land, he was in occupation of the property as tenant under M.C.Bhaskar.

He further claimed that on coming into force of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1974 ('the Act, 1974' for short) under order dated 19.02.1977 the occupancy rights were granted to him by the land Tribunal.

5. Having regard to the rival claims, the first respondent acting under Section 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act referred the matter to the Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division), Bengaluru Rural District.

sentences.text: On issuance of notice by the Transferee Court, the parties appeared.
Only claimant Nos.1 and 3 filed claim statements and other claimants did not file any claim statement.
Claimant No.6 by filing memo dated 23.01.2003 submitted that he has no interest in the property.
7. Claimant No.3 M.C Bhaskar died on 12.01.2005.
Claimant No.3(d) and claimant No.3(b) were examined as PWs.1 and 4, claimant No.5 was examined as PW.2 and claimant No.1 was examined as PW.3 before the Reference Court.

Claimant No.1 relied Exs.P1 to 13, claimant Nos.3(d) &
(b) and claimant No.5 relied Exs.P14 to 21.
One Chikkanarayanappa filed I.A.No.1 before the Reference Court under Order 1 Rule 10(2) CPC to implead him as respondent No.2.
But he did not pursue that.
Therefore, while passing the impugned order, the said application was rejected.

8. The Reference Court on recording the evidence and on hearing the parties declared that claimant No.1 Doddashamanna is entitled to receive the entire compensation and rejected reference petition with respect to claimant No.2, legal heirs of claimant Nos.3 and claimant Nos. 4 to 6.

The reference Court relying on proceedings in LRF No.5/1974-75 which was marked at Ex.P19, the order of Assistant Commissioner Ex.P1 and admissions of PW.2 and PW.4 held that claimant No.1 was the tenant under claimant No.3 and he was so declared by the land Tribunal Devanahalli.
9. Claimant No.3(d) challenges the said order in the above appeal.
Though claimant No.1 was the contesting party, he did not appear before this Court.
The other claimant Nos.3(b), (c) and (e) sail with claimant No.3(d) i.e., the appellant herein.

Submission of Sri. C.Shankar Reddy learned counsel for the appellant-claimants No.3(d).
10.
Ex.P15 shows that only Mangala Gowramma, Kamalamma and claimant No.3 were the owners of the land in question.
The Reference Court committed error in appreciation of Exs.P1 and 19 and the depositions of PWs.2 and 4 in holding that claimant No.1 was declared to be tenant.
Ex.P19 is not a speaking order.
That was contrary to Section 77 of the Act, 1974 and Rule Nos.17 & 19 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Rules, 1974 ('the Rules' for short).
The proceedings under Sections 30 & 31 of the Act are in the nature of the suit.
Therefore, the Reference Court shall decide the title of the parties as if adjudicating the title of the parties in a suit.
The impugned order suffers perversity and illegality.

11. In support of his submission he relies on the following judgments is as follows:
 (i) Purandara Lagama Ingale & Ors Vs Land  Tribunal, Raibag & Ors1  (ii) Rudregowda & others Vs State of Karnataka &
 Others2

sentences.text: Sri .B.R.Srinivasa Gowda, learned Counsel for respondent No.1-the Special Land Acquisition Officer submits that respondent No.1 has already deposited the award amount and abides by the order that may be passed by this Court.
Analysis 14.
The parties are not in dispute on the issue that land bearing Sy.No.32 measuring 4 acres of Anneshwara village was granted to claimant No.3-Bhaskara by order of the Land Tribunal dated 15.02.1962.
Claimant No.1 contended that after such grant he was cultivating the land under claimant.No.3 as the tenant.
He filed an application before the Land tribunal, Devanahalli claiming the occupancy rights under the provisions of the Act, 1974 claiming himself to be the Tenant.
15. There is no dispute that after coming into force of the Act, 1974 the tenanted lands vest in the Government.
The occupant has to seek registration of his rights.
Respondent No.3 did not file any application before the Land Tribunal claiming the occupancy rights.
It was only claimant No.1 who filed declaration on 19.01.1977 claiming the occupancy rights.
The Tribunal conducted an enquiry on the application of claimant No.1.
The claim petition was in respect of three holdings in Sy.No.32 standing in the name of one Kamalamma, M.C.Bhaskar (claimant No.3(d)) and Mangala Gowramma.
The total extent of the said land was 12 acres.

The land standing in the name of each of those holders was 4 acres in that entire Sy.No.32.
16.
Claimant No.1 relied on Ex.P12 & Ex.P19 i.e., the proceedings in LRF No.5/1974-75.
Those documents show that claimant No.1 filed declaration seeking grant of occupancy rights.
The Land Tribunal held enquiry.
The order sheet dated 19.01.1977 in LRF No.5/1974-75 states that claimant No.3- Bhaskar admitted that claimant No.1 is the tenant under him.

Admitting that, Bhaskar,
Mangala Gowramma and claimant No.1 subscribed their signatures in the order sheet dated 19.01.1977.

The proceedings dated 19.02.1977 in Exs.P12 and P19 show that the Land Tribunal enquired the parties to the proceedings and recorded that Bhaskar-claimant No.3 admitted that claimant No.1 was cultivating 4 acres of land since 5/6 years prior thereto.

Recording that said statement and considering the same, the Land Tribunal passed order granting occupancy rights in favor of claimant No.1 for 4 acres of land in Sy.No.32 which was held by Bhaskar prior thereto.

In their William Rathnaraj vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 13 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150404369/
5 - 10 - evidence before the Reference Court, PW.2 claims that he was friend of Bhaskar since 50 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.4 was the daughter of claimant No.3-Bhaskar.

Both of them admitted the signatures of Bhaskar in Exs.P12 and P19.
17.

Much was sought to be argued before this Court that the proceedings in LRF No.5/1974-75 are not in accordance with the provisions of the Act, 1974 and no enquiry was conducted as contemplated under Section 77 of the Act, 1974 and Rules 17 & 19 of the Rules.
18.
The validity of the proceedings was not questioned either in the statement of objections of Mr.Bhaskar filed before respondent No.1 nor in the claim statement made before the Reference Court.
As against that claimant No.3 denied the claim of claimant No.1 on the ground of identity of the property.
He claimed that the said 4 acres in respect of which the Land Tribunal had granted occupancy rights was not his land and that belonged to Mangala Gowramma.
19. Section 77 of the Act, 1974 relates to the enquiries concerning the surplus land vested in the State Government.
Therefore, the said provision is not applicable to the present - 11 - enquiry in question.

Rule 17 of the Rules relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant himself state that the said proceedings are summary in nature as contemplated under Section 34 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964.
Assuming for arguments sake that there was any irregularity in passing the order in Exs.P12 and P19, that order was passed as long back as in the year 19.02.1977.
Till filing of the claim petition in the year 2002 or even till this day, claimant No.3 or his heirs did not challenge that order.
It was contended that since no enquiry was conducted as per the provisions of the Act, 1974, the order is void abinitio.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgments in Krishnadevi Malchand Kamathia Vs Bombay Environmental Action Group7 and Board of Trustees of Port of Kandla Vs Hargovind jasraf,8 has held that even if a party finds that an order is illegal or is a nullity, unless he challenges the same and the same is set aside by the Court of competent jurisdiction, it is not open to the party to claim that the order is a nullity.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. The reading of aforesaid judgments referred by the learned counsel for the appellant supra, show that in those (2011) 3 SCC 363 (2013)3 SCC 182 - 12 - cases the aggrieved parties had challenged the order of the Land Tribunal before this Court by filing the writ petition and not the collateral proceedings.
Therefore, the said judgments cannot be justifiably applied to the facts of the present case.

sentences.text: It is also to be noted that based on the order of the Tahasildar, Devanahalli in RRT DS No.18/2002-03 dated 20.11.2003 directed to enter the name of claimant No.1 to the disputed land.
Bhaskar-claimant No.3 challenged that order before the Assistant Commissioner, Doddaballapura in RA No.3/2004-05.
The Assistant Commissioner by order Ex.P1 dated 17.02.2007 considering merits of the case dismissed the said appeal.
Neither claimant No.3 nor his heirs challenged the said order.
Therefore, the said order attained finality.
Exs . P2
to P5 the RTC of the disputed land for the year 1988-1989 to 2000-2001 show that for all those years claimant No.1 was shown as the cultivator of the land.
It was contended that Exs.P2 to P5 or Ex.P1 are not the documents of title.
No doubt they may not be the documents of title, but they were based on Exs.P12 & 19.
Section 133 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964 confers the presumption with regard to those entries unless they are lawfully substituted.
In this case claimant No.3 - 13 - sought to set aside those entries and challenged the legality of those entries, but failed.

Therefore,
the presumption conferred under Section 133 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act stood further confirmed by the order of Assistant Commissioner- Ex.P1.
23.

The Reference Court taking into consideration all such materials, on sound appreciation of the evidence and the relevant law rejected the claim of claimant No.3 and his heirs and declared that claimant No.3 is not entitled to receive the compensation.
There is no illegality or impropriety in the said order.
The appeal deserves no merit.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed with costs.
